🤖 AutoDev has picked up this issue and started working on it.

**Task ID:** `2e1b2262c967d90d`
**Working branch:** `bugfix/autodev-2538-20261023114157826`
**Target branch:** `latest dev* branch`
**Workflow:** opsp (analysis → coding → testing → PR)

I will post the PR link here once done. If I need more information, I will ask in the comments.

Independent verification from a 2.0.20 + DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 deployment (Linux, node v22.23.1):

- Confirmed the bug exactly as described: every turn that triggers a recall injection fails with 0-token output and `SessionFormatError: format v4 message requires a producer-owned source kind`; the on-disk v4 session file stays clean (rejection happens at runtime adoption), and `~/.dsh/storages/session_projcache` snapshots are also clean.
- Patched the installed 2.0.20 dist locally at both sites (`adapters/deepseek-harness/index.ts` recall message, `adapters/deepseek-harness/host-llm.ts` `toDshMessage`), changing `kind: "plugin"` → `kind: "memos-local-memory"`. After `systemctl --user restart` the same prompt that previously died instantly ran a full multi-tool turn (including a `memos_get` tool call) with zero `SessionFormatError` in the journal.
- Note for the PR: the adapter's own consumer `isUserMessage` (bridge) only requires `source.kind` to be a string, so any producer-owned kind works; your `plugin:memos-local-memory` choice is fine. One caveat: if the published fix lands in a new release, users on 2.0.20 who hand-patched `dist/` (like us) will need to re-apply or reinstall, since a profile `pnpm install` will overwrite the patch — worth a line in the release notes.
- Also observed on this deployment (possibly related, possibly separate): intermittent `MEMOS_DSH_HOST_LLM_TIMEOUT after 2000ms` / `fetch failed` from the host-LLM bridge during retrieval — memory recall still works but degraded. Happy to provide journal excerpts if useful.
